text:
sophia_platform: heads up — in the latency dashboard I'm seeing p95 for /v1/generate trending slightly down but p99 has these sudden micro-spikes. anyone else?
metrics-bot: automated alert: p99 spike detected on /v1/generate at 11:03 UTC, delta +420ms vs baseline :warning:
ethan_sre: saw that. quick check: does this line up with the quota-rewrite rollout? we moved rate-limiter earlier today.
nina_prod: that rollout landed ~10:45. we switched some callers to the new async fanout path (fanout-v2). could be related.
igor_backend: can you share a sample query of the telemetry that shows the split by fanout?
sophia_platform: putting a quick query here — this is the aggregator I used to compare percentiles by route and fanout tag:
```sql
SELECT fanout, percentile(50, latency_ms) AS p50, percentile(95, latency_ms) AS p95, percentile(99, latency_ms) AS p99
FROM request_latency
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND ts >= now() - interval '15 minutes'
GROUP BY fanout;
```
ethan_sre: nice. my immediate hypothesis: p95 is dominated by short-running majority on the new path (good), but the p99 picks up a tiny tail from legacy sync path retries or second-stage reranker calls. overall median can shift independent of tail.
nina_prod: agree — fanout-v2 batches more requests which reduces p50/p95, but we still have a few old callers hitting fanout-v1 that trigger extra hop (reranker).
igor_backend: i ran the query against raw samples. quick dump: fanout-v2 p95=130ms p99=310ms, fanout-v1 p95=220ms p99=1200ms. tiny volume from v1 but huge tail.
sophia_platform: aha. so the aggregation across fanouts without showing weighted-sample counts masks the tail influence from low-volume path. dashboard shows combined p95=140ms and p99=340ms which reads contradictory at glance.
ethan_sre: classic sample-origin confusion. UI shows percentiles but not the underlying sample counts by bucket. we should surface sample_count and a small "source breakdown" tooltip.
metrics-bot: suggestion: emit sample_count_by_fanout and include a tiny sparkline per fanout in the tooltip.
nina_prod: also worth checking if retries are included. are we aggregating with `include_retries=true` anywhere? retries could inflate p99 without affecting p95 much.
igor_backend: runs another quick check: retries are included by default in this view. filtering retries out -> global p99 drops from 340ms to 285ms. still elevated due to v1.
sophia_platform: proposed fixes: (1) add sample_count and retry_ratio to the top-level percentile card, (2) default the combo view to hide fanouts with sample_count < 1% (or gray them), (3) add an explanation line under percentiles: "percentiles are aggregated across fanouts; low-volume fanouts can dominate tails."
ethan_sre: +1. also we should make the console query exampleable for product folks: toggles for `include_retries` and `sample_origin` (fanout/tag).
nina_prod: small UX ask: when you hover p99, show the top-3 contributors to the tail (fanout, retry, reranker) with counts. helps triage.
igor_backend: i can add a backend flag for top-contributors endpoint in the telemetry service. will prototype tomorrow.
sophia_platform: i'll open a short RFC and link it here. tagging igor and ethan to own the backend + UX. @igor_backend @ethan_sre :point_up:
ethan_sre: acked. can you add a short runbook note? e.g., "if p95 and p99 diverge across endpoint, check sample_origin and retries". keep it copyable.
sophia_platform: will add runbook blurb to the RFC and put a quick dashboard annotation for today's rollback window.
metrics-bot: note logged: ISSUE-4523 created — "dashboard: surface sample counts + tail contributors for combined percentiles" https://issues.internal/4523
sophia_platform: thanks. we'll track in the rollout and follow up after igor's prototype. :thumbsup:
